sources.title: Towards Timing Isolation for Mixed-Criticality Communication in Software-Defined Vehicles
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors propose timing isolation across middleware, Linux network stack and NIC hardware for Ethernet communication among mixed-criticality applications on centralized Linux-based automotive control units.
claims.context: Architecture description from the primary abstract.

claims.text: The design combines a fixed-priority non-preemptive publisher scheduler, XDP fast-path delivery for high-priority traffic, and a dedicated NIC queue for real-time traffic in a DDS-based system.
The authors report consistent and predictable real-time latencies even under heavy best-effort interference.
claims.context: Abstract-level result without reconstructed distributions/test conditions.

limitations.text: The primary abstract does not expose hardware, Linux/kernel/NIC versions, traffic load, latency/jitter distributions, CPU cost, or comparison baselines needed for complete performance verification.
The demonstrated architecture is DDS/Linux/XDP/NIC-queue specific; portability to other middleware, kernels and NICs requires separate evidence.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Towards Timing Isolation for Mixed-Criticality Communication in Software-Defined Vehicles; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The primary v2 page verifies the three-layer timing-isolation architecture and qualitative evaluation claim, but detailed performance setup/results require full-paper inspection.

editorial.why_now_note: Timing isolation is a central architectural constraint when mixed-criticality functions share centralized Linux/HPC networking resources.
editorial.rationale: The layered DDS/Linux/XDP/NIC-queue design is highly relevant to centralized mixed-criticality compute, but quantitative evaluation details were not available in the primary HTML view used here.
